newsitem.title: CHINA: U.S. official says "encouraged" by China on arms.
newsitem.headline: U.S. official says "encouraged" by China on arms.

text.p: A senior U.S. arms control official said on Tuesday she was encouraged by China's efforts to implement an accord barring exports to unsafeguarded nuclear facilities.
"I am encouraged by the steps the Chinese are taking," U.S. Undersecretary of State Lynn Davis told reporters.
Davis was referring to China's efforts to implement an agreement reached in May following U.S. accusations that Beijing had exported ring magnets used in nuclear reactors to Pakistan.
China and Pakistan have denied the charges.
The U.S. has said it believed China's central government was unaware of the exports.

Davis, who is responsible for arms control issues, said ensuring practical implementation of the May accord would be necessary before the U.S. could relax curbs on peaceful nuclear cooperation with China.
She made the remarks after two days of talks on arms control issues, including North Korea and Iran, with Chinese officials.
China also raised the issue of U.S. arms sales to Taiwan, Davis said, without giving further details.
China's foreign ministry spokesman Cui Tiankai said that the key issue for Beijing was U.S. arms sales to Taiwan.
The U.S. had exported large numbers of advanced weapons to Taiwan and Beijing hoped Washington would pay attention to its concerns, Cui told reporters.
China and Taiwan have been rivals since the end of the Chinese civil war in 1949. Beijing regards Taiwan as a renegade province and has not ruled out the use of force to recover the island.
In August, the U.S. Defence Department notified Congress it would sell Stinger missiles and launchers to Taiwan, prompting angry protests from Beijing.
Taiwan said in September it would place Patriot defence missiles into service in 1999 under a deal reached with the U.S. manufacturer in 1993.
